title: The Mother Superior
text: An abbess of the Apostate Court holds an audience in a rotting garden, enthroned among dead roses, her habit embroidered with inverted holy signs. Her nuns stand silent in rows. She will speak, she says, only to someone born under the Empress.

options.label: The Empress's child kneels before her and speaks, as she asked.

outcomes.text: She blesses them in the old rite, from before the Court turned. Her hand is cold on their brow, and the cold stays a while.

options.label: The wisest questions her about the Court, and what it worships now.

outcomes.text: She tells of the Court's schism and who began it, and smiles at the end, as if the tale were a gift. It may be a warning.
She calls the guards, and her smile never changes.

options.label: Seize her on her throne of roses, before her silent nuns can close ranks.

outcomes.text: Her nuns fight like cats, and never make a sound. The roses are wet when it is over.
